title: Open House Finance Flyer: neutralize a mixed-light open-house gallery to the in-frame grey card, author a black + brass/gold look from scratch, vectorize the wordmark, and data-merge one press-ready page per price scenario from an authored InDesign template
grounding_note: ADAPTED from a real Upwork brief (a Northern-California mortgage lender wanting an editable, print-and-digital 'Open House Finance Flyer' package: sophisticated / luxury-but-approachable / clean-and-modern, black-white-with-brass/gold accents, with easily editable property photos, purchase price, monthly-payment scenarios, down-payment options, appreciation projections, QR codes and contact info). ALL identifying detail is laundered to fiction: the lender is the invented 'KESTREL HOME LENDING', and the market is the fictional 'Calderon County' with the invented towns Rosewood, Vandermeer and Belhaven — no real person, brand, org or place survives. The source names Canva (out of scope), so the deliverable is recast as the Adobe production work that legitimately sits UNDER such a package: (a) taking a real open-house shoot — a hero exterior plus interior room frames shot across one afternoon under badly mismatched light, each carrying a photographer's grey reference card in a corner — and driving the whole gallery to ONE neutral white point and ONE house 'luxury' look; (b) authoring that black + brass/gold look from tone/colour primitives (not a canned preset); (c) prepping and vectorizing the flat wordmark for crisp print; and (d) exporting the front/back flyer and running a genuine InDesign data-merge that binds the price-scenario CSV — including a per-row property-photo image column — into the lender's own authored .indd template, one record per page. The authored .indd and the CSV are declared client-supplied inputs because the connector exports/merges genuine authored documents; it never composes a layout or a merge target from scratch. The CSV's @PropertyPhoto column names the agent's OWN graded output files by a stated naming convention — this is standard InDesign image-merge behaviour (the roster references the graded files the agent produces and uploads), not a defect. Placeholder addresses and figures are illustrative.
one_line_ask: Neutralize a mixed-light open-house photo gallery to the grey card in each frame BY EYE, hold every shot to one common white point and one authored black + brass/gold look, produce the hero's banner and cut-out variants, colour-match the loan-officer headshot without turning skin orange, vectorize the wordmark, then export the authored InDesign flyer and data-merge the price-scenario CSV (whose @PropertyPhoto column names your graded frames) into one print-ready page per scenario.
full_brief:
I run Kestrel Home Lending and I'm the go-to financing name across Calderon County (Rosewood, Vandermeer, Belhaven). I'm building an 'Open House Finance Flyer' package — front and back, print and digital — and I need the Adobe production pieces done right. The look is non-negotiable: sophisticated, luxury-but-approachable, clean and modern, black and white with brass/gold accents, the kind of thing a Bay-Area buyer trusts.

Here's the problem. My photographer shot the open house across one afternoon, room to room, under whatever light each space happened to have — some window light, some lamps, some overhead fixtures — and a couple of the frames came out too dark or too bright. Straight out of the folder the gallery is a mismatched jumble: no two frames look like they belong to the same set. I'm not going to tell you what's wrong with each shot — that's your job to see. What I know is this: every frame has my photographer's grey card clipped in one corner, and that card is your anchor. I need the entire gallery to read as ONE set: neutral, matched, no frame drifting warm or cool against the others, then all of them carrying the same brass/gold house look — warm metallic highlights, deep clean blacks, and NOT a garish orange lawn or orange skin. If one frame still looks like a different room on a different day, it's wrong. When you deliver, tell me the exact per-frame settings you landed on so I can trust the set is actually matched and not just eyeballed.

Then: from the graded hero I need a wide banner crop for the flyer's top band (the house can't be squeezed or cut off) and a clean cut-out of the house on transparency for the social variant. My headshot was shot cool and flat in a studio — bring it onto the same look so it sits beside the property, but keep my skin looking like skin, not orange. My wordmark is a flat charcoal PNG on an off-white background; I need it as a crisp SVG that holds up at any print size and on the tiny contact strip. Finally, export my front/back flyer from the InDesign template I'm giving you, and run the data-merge so each price scenario in my CSV becomes its own print-ready page — purchase price, down-payment options, monthly payment, five-year appreciation, the address, AND the matching property photo dropped into the page from the CSV's photo column. The template and the CSV are mine and already built for the merge; the CSV's photo column just names the graded frames you produce, so name and hand them over so they resolve. Don't rebuild the template or the roster.

Acceptance: every delivered frame's grey card looks neutral and the set shares one white point; the brass/gold look is consistent across all of them; the hero banner is a reframe of real pixels (never stretched or upscaled); skin stays natural; the wordmark traces clean with no soft halo; and the merged PDF has exactly one page per CSV row with the right photo on each.

inputs.name: exterior_hero_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal hi-res real-estate exterior listing photo of a modern two-story home, beige stucco and dark trim, manicured lawn and driveway, shot handheld so the horizon is tilted about 4 degrees, MIXED late-afternoon light: warm direct sun on the right facade, cool blue open-shade on the left, some blown-out white sky highlights and slightly muddy shadows. A neutral 18% grey photographer's reference card is clipped in the lower-left corner of the frame. Real roof-tile and stucco texture, documentary not CGI, no people, no text overlay. Shot on a real camera at roughly 4000 px long edge.
inputs.realism_notes: Hero of the gallery. Tilt gives auto_straighten real work; the warm-sun/cool-shade split and blown sky make the white-balance-to-card correction genuinely per-frame, not a slider nudge. The corner grey card is the neutral anchor and gets cropped out on delivery. Declared at camera scale (~4000 px) so every downscale-only print crop is reachable without upscaling.

inputs.name: kitchen_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal real-estate interior photo of a modern kitchen with quartz island and stainless appliances, lit mostly by warm tungsten recessed pot lights so the whole frame has a strong orange cast, a cooler daylight window on one side creating a mixed colour-temperature split. A neutral 18% grey reference card sits propped on the countertop in the lower-right corner. Real material texture, slightly flat contrast, un-graded, no people, no text. ~4000 px long edge.
inputs.realism_notes: Strong warm/orange tungsten cast that must be pulled back to neutral against the card — a DIFFERENT correction from the exterior. Mixed window light means a uniform batch WB fails. The planted cast is NOT named in the brief; the agent must diagnose it from the card.

inputs.name: living_room_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal real-estate interior photo of a bright living room lit only by cool north-facing window shade, giving a noticeable blue/cool cast, sofa and rug, slightly low contrast. A neutral 18% grey reference card is clipped to the corner of the coffee table. Real fabric and wood texture, un-graded catalog look, no people, no text. ~4000 px long edge.
inputs.realism_notes: Cool/blue member of the set — needs warming toward the same neutral the warm frames are cooled toward, so the batch genuinely converges from both directions. Cast not named in the brief; diagnosed off the card.

inputs.name: primary_suite_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal real-estate interior photo of a primary bedroom suite lit dimly by a single warm bedside lamp, underexposed with muddy shadows and a warm amber cast, some detail lost in the dark corners. A neutral 18% grey reference card rests on the nightstand. Real bedding and wood texture, un-graded, no people, no text. ~4000 px long edge.
inputs.realism_notes: Underexposed AND warm — exercises exposure/shadow lift on top of the WB correction, so this frame's apply_adjustments call carries a different exposure move than the others. Cast not named in the brief.

inputs.name: guest_bath_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal real-estate interior photo of a guest bathroom lit by overhead fluorescent tubes giving a green/magenta cast, tile and mirror, flat even light. A neutral 18% grey reference card is propped on the vanity. Real tile and chrome texture, un-graded, no people, no text. ~4000 px long edge.
inputs.realism_notes: Green fluorescent cast — the tint (green/magenta) axis matters here, not just temperature, so a temperature-only correction leaves the card non-neutral. Forces the agent to use tint, not just warmth. Cast not named in the brief; the two-axis diagnosis is the agent's.

inputs.name: patio_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal real-estate exterior photo of a backyard patio at deep golden hour, very warm low sun, long shadows, high dynamic range with bright sky and dark foreground. A neutral 18% grey reference card is clipped to a patio chair in the corner. Real stone and greenery texture, un-graded, no people, no text. ~4000 px long edge.
inputs.realism_notes: The warmest, highest-contrast frame. Neutralizing to the card here while keeping the golden-hour appeal from looking dead is the hardest single WB judgement in the set. Cast not named in the brief.

inputs.name: loan_officer_headshot_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal professional corporate headshot of a friendly mid-40s loan officer, business-casual blazer no tie, neutral grey studio backdrop, soft key light that is slightly cool and flat, real skin pores and a few flyaway hairs, natural catchlights, candid approachable expression, shot on 85mm, no retouching yet, no text. ~4000 px long edge.
inputs.realism_notes: Cool/flat studio look so the match-to-house-look step is meaningful. No grey card here (studio), so it must be matched to the gallery's neutral target BY EYE and the brass/gold look applied WITHOUT pushing skin orange — the constraint that makes it hard and the divergent-treatment member of the triage (property frames get the full look, skin gets it held back).

inputs.name: kestrel_wordmark.png
inputs.gen_prompt: Flat 2D brand wordmark logo on a plain light background (NOT transparent), the text 'KESTREL HOME LENDING' in an elegant high-contrast serif with a small kestrel-and-key monogram to the left, single solid dark charcoal colour, crisp edges but rendered as an ordinary PNG so the letter edges carry a faint anti-aliased grey halo and the background is a solid off-white, centred with generous padding, no gradients, no photographic background.
inputs.realism_notes: Flat single-colour text mark so image_vectorize can produce a clean SVG — but delivered on a solid off-white ground with soft anti-aliased edges, so it MUST be crisped and knocked to transparency before tracing or the trace picks up a grey halo and a filled rectangle. gemini-3-pro-image for legible typography.

inputs.name: open_house_finance_flyer.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED client asset (not model-generated): a genuine 2-page (front/back) US-Letter InDesign template for an 'Open House Finance Flyer', authored as a SINGLE-RECORD data-merge document — ONE scenario record's worth of fields, so the merge emits one page per row. Front: a wide hero image frame in the top band, a brass/gold rule, a headline area, a wordmark frame and a loan-officer headshot frame. Back: a tagged payment-scenario block carrying LIVE InDesign data-merge text fields <<PurchasePrice>>, <<DownPaymentOptions>>, <<MonthlyPayment>>, <<AppreciationProjection>>, <<PropertyAddress>>, PLUS a data-merge IMAGE frame bound to an @-prefixed image column @PropertyPhoto, and a QR/contact strip. Saved as a real .indd with live merge placeholders and named frames.
inputs.realism_notes: Declared CLIENT-AUTHORED because the connector only EXPORTS or MERGES a genuine authored .indd/.idml — it cannot compose a layout, and a PDF converted via convert_pdf_to_indd will NOT bind merge fields. Single-record template: document_merge_data_layout emits ONE RECORD PER PAGE (N rows -> N pages), so this holds exactly one record's worth of fields and one @PropertyPhoto image frame; a multi-record N-up grid is not producible and is not attempted.

inputs.name: payment_scenarios.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a realistic CSV whose header row is exactly: PurchasePrice,DownPaymentOptions,MonthlyPayment,AppreciationProjection,PropertyAddress,@PropertyPhoto  — with 6 data rows for Calderon County homes priced $625,000 to $1,150,000; DownPaymentOptions like '5% / 10% / 20%'; MonthlyPayment as realistic P&I+escrow at ~6.8% APR; AppreciationProjection as a five-year percentage range; PropertyAddress as plausible Rosewood / Vandermeer / Belhaven street addresses; and @PropertyPhoto naming the agent's graded output files by the fixed convention — row 1 @exterior_hero_graded.jpg, row 2 @kitchen_graded.jpg, row 3 @living_room_graded.jpg, row 4 @primary_suite_graded.jpg, row 5 @guest_bath_graded.jpg, row 6 @patio_graded.jpg — one graded gallery frame per scenario page.
inputs.realism_notes: Column headers must exactly match the .indd's <<merge fields>>, and @PropertyPhoto MUST be @-prefixed. The @PropertyPhoto entries are a FORWARD REFERENCE to the agent's OWN graded output filenames (produced later in the chain, then uploaded) — this is standard InDesign image-merge behaviour, not a defect: the roster names the files the merge will resolve to the uploaded graded assets. The agent must name its six graded frames to this convention and upload them so the @ column binds. A text-only vector merge, or a header without the @, would silently drop the photo — the trap.

outputs.name: gallery_graded_x6
outputs.spec: The six open-house frames (exterior hero, kitchen, living room, primary suite, guest bath, patio), each neutralized BY EYE to its in-frame grey card so the card looks neutral and all six share ONE common white point, then carrying ONE authored black + brass/gold look (warm metallic highlights, deep clean blacks, restrained greens so lawn/foliage is not garish), grey card cropped out, sRGB JPEG, long edge sized to the flyer's frames, named to the CSV convention (exterior_hero_graded.jpg, kitchen_graded.jpg, living_room_graded.jpg, primary_suite_graded.jpg, guest_bath_graded.jpg, patio_graded.jpg). A matched set, not six separate edits. The agent reports the final per-frame temperature/tint/exposure settings it APPLIED (an applied-settings log, not a measurement). Acceptance (grader-checked, on the output): each delivered card's mid-grey patch reads neutral within ~±3 8-bit levels of channel spread and all six share one white point.

outputs.name: hero_property_banner.jpg
outputs.spec: Wide banner-ratio reframe of the graded exterior hero for the flyer's full-width top band — a horizontal slice through house/sky/foreground so the house is not distorted or dropped; produced by crop-and-resize of real pixels only, never larger than the source in the widened dimension, no invented/outpainted pixels.

outputs.name: property_cutout.png
outputs.spec: The graded hero's house isolated from its background to a transparent PNG, for the digital/social flyer variant.

outputs.name: headshot_matched.jpg
outputs.spec: The loan-officer headshot neutralized off its cool/flat studio cast to the gallery's white point and carrying the same brass/gold house look at REDUCED strength on skin (skin stays natural, not orange), sRGB JPEG, sized for the flyer headshot frame.

outputs.name: wordmark.svg
outputs.spec: Clean single-colour vectorized wordmark, no anti-aliased grey halo and no filled background rectangle (crisped and knocked to transparency before tracing), scalable SVG for print and the small contact strip.

outputs.name: open_house_finance_flyer.pdf
outputs.spec: Front/back Open House Finance Flyer exported from the authored .indd, US-Letter, print-ready PDF (export only; layout is authored, not composed here).

outputs.name: payment_scenarios_merged.pdf
outputs.spec: Multi-page print-ready PDF from the InDesign data-merge — exactly one page per CSV scenario row (page count == row count == 6), each page carrying that row's purchase price, down-payment options, monthly payment, appreciation projection, address, AND the matching graded property photo placed from the @PropertyPhoto column. Acceptance (grader-checked): page-count == row-count and the correct graded frame on each page.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: exterior_hero_raw.jpg, kitchen_raw.jpg, living_room_raw.jpg, primary_suite_raw.jpg, guest_bath_raw.jpg, patio_raw.jpg, loan_officer_headshot_raw.jpg, kestrel_wordmark.png, open_house_finance_flyer.indd, payment_scenarios.csv
connector_workflow.note: Single batch upload of the six open-house frames, the headshot, the flat wordmark PNG, the authored flyer .indd and the scenario CSV into the working project so every downstream tool has real asset references. Plumbing — not a difficulty step.
Fix the ~4-degree tilted horizon on the exterior hero. Deciding this is part of the job: only the hero is tilted; the interior frames are level, so this runs once, not across the batch.

Neutralize the hero to its corner grey card BY EYE: dial temperature AND tint until the card looks neutral (the warm-sun/cool-shade split means this frame's WB is unique to it), pull highlights/whites down to recover the blown sky, lift shadows off the muddy blacks, set clean rich blacks. This decision is driven off THIS frame's card, not copied from any other frame. Wrong direction/amount here leaves the delivered card visibly tinted against the rest of the set — the visible failure mode of the cross-asset gate. Report the temperature/tint/exposure applied.

Author the house look on the neutralized hero via per-hue-band HSL: warm the highlight/yellow-orange band toward brass-gold and hold its saturation so metallic warmth reads without going garish, and pull the green band's saturation down so the lawn/foliage recedes and the palette stays black/white/brass. This split-tone IS the agent's design decision — no preset, no auto_tone. The same authored look is the target for every other frame.

Crop the grey card out of the lower-left corner and reframe to the flyer's print hero ratio, downscale only from the ~4000 px source. Yields the exterior_hero_graded member of gallery_graded_x6 (the name the CSV @PropertyPhoto row 1 references).

Reframe the graded hero into the flyer's wide full-width top-band ratio — a horizontal slice keeping the whole house, crop-and-resize of real pixels only, never larger than the source in the widened dimension (DELIVERABLE: hero_property_banner.jpg). No outpainting/canvas-extend.

Semantically select the house structure on the graded hero ('the two-story house building') as QA evidence of the intended isolation; the maskURI is kept for review (image_remove_background re-detects the subject itself).
Isolate the house to a transparent PNG for the digital/social variant (DELIVERABLE: property_cutout.png). Honest remove_background to transparency — not select->invert->fill.

Neutralize the kitchen to its countertop grey card BY EYE. The agent must diagnose this frame's cast itself: it is strongly warm (tungsten pot lights), so temperature is pulled COOL toward the same neutral target the hero was driven to — the OPPOSITE direction from the living room. Mixed window light means a single global shift must still land the card neutral; a uniform batch setting fails here. Report the applied move.
Apply the SAME authored brass/gold split-tone as the hero (identical hue-band intent) so the kitchen joins the matched set.
Crop the grey card out and size to the flyer frame, downscale only. Member of gallery_graded_x6, named kitchen_graded.jpg (CSV @PropertyPhoto row 2).

Neutralize the living room to its coffee-table grey card BY EYE. Diagnosed by the agent: this frame is cool/blue (north-window shade), so temperature is pushed WARM toward the common neutral — converging on the same white point as the warm frames but from the opposite side. Add a little contrast off its low-contrast base. Report the applied move.
Apply the same authored brass/gold split-tone so the living room matches the set.
Crop the grey card out and size to the flyer frame, downscale only. Member of gallery_graded_x6, named living_room_graded.jpg (CSV @PropertyPhoto row 3).

Neutralize the primary suite to its nightstand grey card AND lift it. Diagnosed by the agent: this frame is dim/underexposed and warm off a lamp, so it needs a positive exposure/shadow lift plus a cool WB move — a different apply_adjustments recipe from every other frame, all still landing the card neutral and the brightness on the set mean. Report the applied move.
Apply the same authored brass/gold split-tone so the suite matches the set.
Crop the grey card out and size to the flyer frame, downscale only. Member of gallery_graded_x6, named primary_suite_graded.jpg (CSV @PropertyPhoto row 4).

Neutralize the guest bath to its vanity grey card BY EYE. Diagnosed by the agent: the cast is green fluorescent, so the correction is primarily on the TINT (green->magenta) axis, not temperature — a temperature-only move would leave the card green. This frame proves the neutralization is a two-axis decision. Report the applied move.
Apply the same authored brass/gold split-tone so the bath matches the set.
Crop the grey card out and size to the flyer frame, downscale only. Member of gallery_graded_x6, named guest_bath_graded.jpg (CSV @PropertyPhoto row 5).

Neutralize the patio to its grey card BY EYE. Diagnosed by the agent: the warmest, highest-dynamic-range frame (deep golden hour), so it needs the strongest cool WB move plus highlight recovery on the bright sky and shadow lift on the dark foreground, all while keeping the card neutral and the brightness on the set mean without killing the golden-hour appeal. Report the applied move.
Apply the same authored brass/gold split-tone so the patio matches the set.

Crop the grey card out and size to the flyer frame, downscale only. Member of gallery_graded_x6, named patio_graded.jpg (CSV @PropertyPhoto row 6). exterior_hero_graded + kitchen/living_room/primary_suite/guest_bath/patio_graded complete the six.

Neutralize the cool/flat studio headshot toward the SAME white point the gallery was driven to — no grey card here, so it is matched to the set's neutral target BY EYE, protecting skin from going cool or waxy. Report the applied move.

Bring the headshot onto the house look, but RESTRAINED: warm the highlight band toward brass far more gently than on the property frames and hold the orange/red (skin) band's saturation DOWN so the loan officer's skin stays natural, not orange. This is the divergent-treatment member of the triage — same target look, deliberately different strength — and matching the look without wrecking skin is the constraint.
Size the matched headshot to the flyer's headshot frame, downscale only (DELIVERABLE: headshot_matched.jpg).

Prep-before-trace step 1: push contrast/clarity and blacks/whites to hard limits so the wordmark's anti-aliased grey halo collapses to pure charcoal-on-white, giving image_vectorize a clean edge to trace instead of a fuzzy one.
Prep-before-trace step 2: crop tight to the mark's bounds, removing the surplus off-white padding.
Prep-before-trace step 3: knock the solid off-white ground to transparency so the trace picks up the LETTERS, not a filled rectangle behind them. Without this the vectorize returns a solid block.

Trace the crisped, knocked-to-transparency single-colour wordmark to a clean scalable SVG (DELIVERABLE: wordmark.svg). Tracing the raw PNG instead would embed the halo and the background block — the prep discipline is the point.

Export the client-authored front/back flyer .indd to a print-ready US-Letter PDF (DELIVERABLE: open_house_finance_flyer.pdf). Export ONLY — the layout is authored by the client; nothing is composed here.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: exterior_hero_graded, kitchen_graded, living_room_graded, primary_suite_graded, guest_bath_graded, patio_graded
connector_workflow.note: Initialize an upload session for the six graded gallery frames so the data-merge can resolve the CSV's @PropertyPhoto column to real asset references. The frames are named to the CSV convention (exterior_hero_graded.jpg ... patio_graded.jpg) so each @PropertyPhoto entry binds to the matching graded file.
Finalize the upload; returns the asset URNs the roster's @PropertyPhoto column resolves to for each scenario row's single-record page.

InDesign data-merge into the AUTHORED single-record .indd (never a convert_pdf_to_indd output — that would not bind): bind each CSV row to the live text fields <<PurchasePrice>>/<<DownPaymentOptions>>/<<MonthlyPayment>>/<<AppreciationProjection>>/<<PropertyAddress>> AND drop that row's graded photo through the @PropertyPhoto image column, producing exactly ONE RECORD PER PAGE (6 rows -> 6 pages). document_merge_data_vector is wrong here — it is text-only and would silently drop the photo. [T]: needs the client's authored template with real fields + @image column.

Export the merged single-record set to a press-ready US-Letter PDF (DELIVERABLE: payment_scenarios_merged.pdf). Acceptance (grader-checked): page-count == CSV row-count == 6, each page carrying the correct graded property photo; if fewer pages, the merge collapsed rows and failed.

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining. One batch upload (1). Hero branch: auto_straighten (2) -> apply_adjustments neutralize-to-card by eye (3) -> adjust_hsl authored brass/gold split-tone (4) -> crop_and_resize print hero (5), which fans out to the banner reframe (6), the QA house selection (7) and the transparent cut-out (8). Five interior/exterior frames each run their OWN apply_adjustments neutralize-to-card (9,12,15,18,21) with a per-frame WB decision the agent diagnoses and that converges on one common white point from different directions (kitchen/patio cooled, living warmed, bath tint-corrected, suite exposure-lifted), then the SAME authored split-tone hsl (10,13,16,19,22) and a card-cropping downscale resize (11,14,17,20,23); exterior_hero_graded plus these five complete gallery_graded_x6, named to the CSV convention. Headshot branch: neutralize to the set white point (24) -> restrained hsl that protects skin (25) -> resize (26). Wordmark branch: crisp (27) -> crop_to_bounds (28) -> remove_background knock-to-transparency (29) -> vectorize (30), the prep-before-trace chain. Document branch, modelled on the passing sibling: render_layout exports the authored .indd flyer (31); the six graded frames are uploaded via asset_initialize_file_upload (32) -> asset_finalize_file_upload (33) so the @PropertyPhoto column resolves; document_merge_data_layout (34) binds the CSV rows + the six graded photos into the SAME authored .indd, one record per page; document_render_layout (35) exports that merged set to the final PDF. Every post-upload step consumes a named prior output; nothing is produced from thin air, and the merge target is the authored .indd, never a PDF conversion.
difficulty_rationale: Depth over breadth: 35 dependent connector calls across 13 distinct Adobe tools, but the difficulty is in the reasoning, not the count. The batch is six genuinely differently-lit frames whose casts are NOT named in the brief — the agent must diagnose each from its in-frame grey card and choose a correction that DIFFERS per frame (two cooled, one warmed, one tint-corrected on the green axis, one exposure-lifted, one heavy golden-hour) yet all converge on ONE common white point and carry ONE authored black + brass/gold look the agent designs from apply_adjustments + per-hue-band adjust_hsl primitives (never a preset or auto_tone). The graded hero is reused three ways (print, banner reframe, transparent cut-out); the headshot must join the look without turning skin orange (a divergent-strength treatment); the wordmark demands prep-before-trace discipline; and the document branch requires the merge to hit the AUTHORED single-record .indd with an @-prefixed image column — one record per page (6 rows -> 6 pages) — not a text-only vector merge and not a PDF-converted target. All headless [C] except the one [T] data-merge, which legitimately needs the client's authored template. No banned capability: no generative fill/expand/outpaint, no upscaling (every crop downscales from ~4000 px sources), no auto_tone/preset as the look, no convert_pdf_to_indd merge target, no image_fill_area, no coordinate layout, and no agent-side pixel/hex/channel measurement anywhere.
hardness_rationale: Failure gate (a craft DECISION with a visible failure mode, not a self-measurement): the gallery is six frames shot under six different lights whose casts the brief does NOT name, and each needs a DIFFERENT correction reasoned BY EYE off its in-frame grey card — some warmed, some cooled, one corrected on the green/magenta tint axis, one exposure-lifted, one heavy golden-hour pulled back — all converging on ONE house white point and ONE authored brass/gold look. The naive path applies a single uniform white-balance/temperature across the whole batch, or reaches for image_apply_preset / image_apply_auto_tone for the 'luxury look'; either leaves the differently-lit frames visibly mismatched (one still orange, one still blue, one still green) — a failure obvious at a glance across the delivered set. The agent never reads a pixel: it neutralises each card by eye and REPORTS the final per-frame temperature/tint/exposure it APPLIED (an applied-settings log), so 'matched' is gradeable without the agent measuring. Human-hard elements: (1) cross-asset white-point + look consistency across six differently-lit frames, each a different move converging on one neutral; (2) an agent-AUTHORED brass/gold split-tone from image_apply_adjustments + per-hue-band image_adjust_hsl (warm highlights, deep blacks, tamed greens), applied at full strength on the property frames but RESTRAINED on the headshot so skin stays natural not orange — a divergent-treatment triage; (3) prep-before-trace vectorize discipline (crisp -> crop-to-bounds -> knock-to-transparency) or the SVG carries a halo and a filled block; (4) merge constraint reasoning — the per-row @PropertyPhoto image column (which names the agent's own graded output files by a stated convention) must bind into the authored single-record .indd via document_merge_data_layout, one record per page, not document_merge_data_vector (text-only, drops the photo) and not a convert_pdf_to_indd target (fields won't bind). The deliberate TRAP: a uniform batch white-balance plus a preset/auto_tone 'grade' looks plausible but fails the neutrality gate on the differently-lit cards; a second trap is a text-only vector merge or a PDF-converted merge target, either of which silently drops the per-row photo. Acceptance (grader-checked on the OUTPUT — the agent never measures): each delivered grey card's mid-grey patch neutral within ~±3 8-bit levels of channel spread and all six sharing one white point; banner reframed from real pixels (never upscaled past source); skin non-orange; wordmark trace halo-free with no background block; merged PDF page-count == CSV row-count (6) with the correct graded photo on each page.
